name: Medium Slate Blue
lede: Medium Slate Blue is a bright, electric blue-violet that exists as a color name because it sits in the X11 color list and, from there, in the CSS color keywords.

sections.title: A list name
sections.body:
Medium Slate Blue is one of the colors in the X11 Color Set, with the hex code #7B68EE [1]. It is also a CSS keyword, `mediumslateblue`, in the extended color list of the W3C's CSS Color Module Level 3 [2]. None of our books says more than that dictionary entry, so who coined the name, and why, is undocumented here [1].

It is a different color from [[medium-purple]] and [[medium-blue]], which sit beside it in the same list [1]. Despite the word *slate*, it has nothing in common with [[slate-grey]], the dull bluish grey of the stone [3].

sections.title: Measured
sections.body: The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would file this swatch under "brilliant violet" (block 206), but at a distance of 10.8 CIEDE2000 units, a loose fit [3]. Its Munsell notation is about 9.5PB 5.1/17.7: a mid-light value with a very high chroma [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this color over at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [4]. In printed English the phrase *medium slate blue* appears from 1920 and peaks in the 1990s [5].

origin.named_after: origin undocumented; an entry in the X11 color list
origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 260

disambiguation.gloss: a dull bluish grey, not a violet blue
